The story

The Tudor trademark was registered in 1926 by Hans Wilsdorf, the founder of Rolex, who established Montres Tudor SA in 1946. The brand's purpose was to offer watches with the quality and dependability of a Rolex but at a more accessible price point. Early models often used Rolex cases and bracelets with third-party Swiss movements. Tudor made a name for itself by producing durable tool watches, becoming the watch of choice for the French Navy and the US Navy. A key turning point for the brand was its modern relaunch, which began around 2010 and was solidified with the introduction of the Heritage Black Bay line in 2012. This collection, which includes models like the Black Bay, Black Bay 58, and Black Bay 54, draws inspiration from Tudor's vintage dive watches, such as the 1954 Oyster Prince Submariner and the 1958 reference 7924 "Big Crown". The brand further diversified the Black Bay line with the Black Bay Chrono, which merges diving and motorsport heritage, and the Black Bay Pro, which is reminiscent of vintage explorer watches. Another significant development was the introduction of the Black Bay Ceramic in 2021, which was the brand's first watch to receive METAS Master Chronometer certification. Today, Tudor stands as an independent and innovative watchmaker, a status cemented by the introduction of its first in-house movement in 2015. The brand's commitment to modern performance is also evident in the Pelagos line, first launched in 2012 as a contemporary dive watch. This collection has expanded to include the more versatile Pelagos 39 and the military-developed Pelagos FXD, which features fixed strap bars and was designed in collaboration with the French Navy.
